summary: Most travelers need a Syrian visa arranged before arrival: the UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all tell their citizens to get one in advance, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain one at Syrian border points. Arab-state citizens have historically entered without a visa. Syria has announced an online eVisa, but its website was not yet taking applications in late September 2026 — confirm how to apply with a Syrian embassy shortly before travel.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 3 months after the date you arrive. Rules are applied inconsistently during the transition, so more validity is safer.

travelInsurance.text: Not checked at the border, but most mainstream travel insurers exclude Syria entirely — specialist conflict-zone cover is the only realistic option.

source.name: Syrian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates

onwardTicket.text: Not systematically checked; overland travelers should nonetheless carry evidence of onward plans and accommodation.

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed amount is published. Border posts have at times required visitors to exchange or show US dollars. Carry cash and expect rules to change without notice.

payments.text: Syria is a cash economy: international cards and ATMs do not work for foreign visitors, so bring everything you will need in US dollars or euros and change small amounts at a time.

safety.text: Syria remains high-risk after more than a decade of war: unexploded ordnance, sporadic fighting, terrorism and arbitrary detention are real dangers, and consular help is minimal — most governments advise against all travel. Security varies sharply by region and can change overnight.

source.name: UK FCDO — Syria travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: Spring and fall are mild across Damascus, the coast and the desert sites; summers are hot and winters can be surprisingly cold, with snow in the hills.

tips.text: Entry rules are changing rapidly under the transitional government — reconfirm your visa, route and permits with a Syrian embassy and a reputable local operator days, not weeks, before travel.
Most governments still advise against all travel to Syria — if you go anyway, use an experienced local guide, share your itinerary with someone at home and register with your embassy where possible.
Travelers with Israeli stamps, visas or any other evidence of travel to Israel are refused entry. Use a clean passport.
Bring US dollars or euros in cash for the entire trip — foreign cards and ATMs do not work, and crisp, undamaged notes get the best rates.
Expect frequent checkpoints between cities. Carry your passport, visa and any permits at all times, and never photograph military or government sites.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Syria?
faq.answer: Almost certainly yes. Unless you hold an Arab-state passport, plan on getting a visa before you travel. The UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments all say their citizens need one in advance, and Canada says non-Arab nationals cannot obtain one at Syrian border points. Syria has announced an online eVisa, but its website was not yet taking applications in late September 2026, so ask a Syrian embassy how to apply.

faq.question: Can I get a Syrian visa on arrival?
faq.answer: Do not plan on it. Visas on arrival at Damascus airport were reported for some Western nationalities in 2025, but the UK, Canadian, German and Australian governments now all say their citizens must have a visa before travel, and Canada states that non-Arab nationals cannot get one at Syrian border points. Arrange the visa through a Syrian embassy before booking.

faq.question: Is Syria safe to visit?
faq.answer: No — most governments advise against all travel. Damascus, Aleppo and the coast are calmer than during the war years, and organized tours do run, but unexploded ordnance, sporadic fighting, terrorism and detention risks remain real, and consular support is minimal. Anyone going should use experienced local guides and follow conditions daily.

faq.question: What money should I use in Syria?
faq.answer: Cash only. Bring US dollars or euros for your whole stay — international cards and ATMs do not work for visitors — and exchange into Syrian pounds in small amounts as needed. Clean, recent-series banknotes are strongly preferred.

faq.question: Can I visit Syria if I have been to Israel?
faq.answer: No. Syria refuses entry to Israeli passport holders and to any traveler whose passport or belongings show evidence of travel to Israel, including stamps from Israeli land borders with Jordan or Egypt. Travel on a clean passport.
